title: Uric Acid Test
attribution: Source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine.
measures: Checks how much uric acid is in a blood or urine sample. Uric acid is a waste product from breaking down purines, and when it builds up in the blood it can form crystals in joints, causing gout.
low: Low blood levels are uncommon and usually do not cause health problems.
high: The body may make too much uric acid, or the kidneys may not remove enough. Eating many high-purine foods such as red meat, certain seafood, alcohol or high-fructose corn syrup can raise levels. Possible causes include gout, kidney disease or stones, certain cancers and their treatments, alcohol use disorder and preeclampsia.
notes: Medicines including aspirin, and niacin, can affect results. A high level does not always mean a condition that needs treatment.
